rename.resolution: re-verdicted `declined` -- same class as the zero-init family, which is already declined; nros_<entity>_<verb> is the C convention and rcl's verb-first ORDER is what we decline, the word itself already matches

why: CORRECTED 2026-09-18 (phase-417 W4.e). Both spellings ship and the correlator buckets this item `same`, which is the opposite of what the row said in BOTH directions: it claimed ours is `rclc_guard_condition_trigger` (nothing defined that symbol) and that a porting user must rewrite `rcl_trigger_guard_condition` (which we have exported all along). `rclc_guard_condition_trigger` is the definition -- `nros_<entity>_<verb>` is our C convention, the same one that makes `c:get_zero_initialized_guard_condition` and `c:get_zero_initialized_publisher` `declined` -- and `rcl_trigger_guard_condition` is kept as a forwarder, not deprecated, because RFC-0089's alias rule makes a name upstream HAS load-bearing rather than a courtesy. So a ported rcl node keeps compiling and loses nothing. Ours half: `c:guard_condition_trigger`. RE-VERDICTED 2026-08-26 (phase-379 W5), was `rename`.
